subject.title: feat(exec): verified-human instruction provenance for sensitive targets

question: What verified-human provenance contract and sensitive-target policy surface should OpenClaw support for exec, outbound messaging, and gateway actions?
rationale: The issue would introduce public security semantics, config/API surface, and compatibility-sensitive enforcement behavior that cannot be safely chosen by automation from source inspection alone.

options.title: Core gateway policy
options.body: Add a core-enforced sensitive-target policy with explicit config/schema, provenance propagation, and stricter approval or denial fallback at the tool/gateway boundary.

options.title: Plugin context first
options.body: First enrich plugin hook context with action classification and provenance, then let a security plugin implement the policy once the SDK contract is accepted.

options.title: Fold into taint umbrella
options.body: Defer this narrower request into the broader persistent-taint and content-derived execution guardrail design so maintainers choose one unified security model.

recommendation.title: Core gateway policy
recommendation.body: Add a core-enforced sensitive-target policy with explicit config/schema, provenance propagation, and stricter approval or denial fallback at the tool/gateway boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The hook contract and before_tool_call security/approval history make this the strongest available owner signal for the policy surface decision.
